requirements.obligation_summary: Ensure products are designed, developed and produced in accordance with Annex I Part I.
Perform product cybersecurity risk assessment and use it across planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance.
Document and maintain the cybersecurity risk assessment over the support period, including applicability and implementation of Annex I requirements.
Include the cybersecurity risk assessment in technical documentation and justify non-applicable essential requirements.
Exercise cybersecurity due diligence when integrating third-party and open-source components.
Notify component maintainers of discovered component vulnerabilities and share relevant fixes/documentation where appropriate.
Systematically document product cybersecurity aspects and vulnerabilities, and update risk assessment where applicable.
Handle product/component vulnerabilities effectively for the support period and determine/document an appropriate support period.
Keep each support-period security update available for at least ten years or the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer.
For substantially modified software versions, satisfy conditions governing support of the latest version and free user access.
When historical software archives are maintained, clearly warn users about unsupported-version risks.
Before market placement, prepare technical documentation, perform conformity assessment, draw up EU declaration and affix CE marking after demonstrated conformity.
Retain technical documentation and EU declaration for at least ten years after market placement or the support period, whichever is longer.
Maintain production-series conformity and account for product/process/standards/certification/common-specification changes.
Provide product type, batch, serial number or another identification element.
Provide manufacturer identity and contact details as required with the product/packaging/documentation.
Designate an easily identifiable single point of contact that enables direct and rapid user communication, including vulnerability reporting.
Provide Annex II user information/instructions in understandable form and retain availability for the required period.
Clearly communicate support-period end date and, where technically feasible, notify users at end of support.
Provide the EU declaration of conformity or a simplified declaration with access to the full declaration.
When non-conformity is known or reasonably suspected, immediately take corrective measures, withdrawal or recall as appropriate.
On reasoned market-surveillance request, provide conformity information/documentation and cooperate on risk elimination measures.
Notify any actively exploited vulnerability of which the manufacturer becomes aware to the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA through the Single Reporting Platform.
Submit AEV early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, including affected Member States where applicable.
Submit AEV notification without undue delay and within 72 hours with product/exploit/vulnerability and mitigation information.
Submit AEV final report no later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available.
Include vulnerability severity and impact in the AEV final report.
Include available information concerning malicious actors exploiting the vulnerability.
Include details of security updates or other corrective measures made available.
Notify any severe incident affecting product security to the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA through the Single Reporting Platform.
Submit severe-incident early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours, including malicious-act suspicion and affected Member States where applicable.
Submit severe-incident notification without undue delay and within 72 hours with nature, initial assessment and mitigation information.
Submit severe-incident final report within one month after the 72-hour notification.
Final incident report contains detailed incident severity and impact.
Final incident report identifies likely threat type or root cause.
Final incident report records applied and ongoing mitigation measures.
Classify as severe where availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of sensitive/important data or functions is negatively affected or capable of being affected.
Classify as severe where malicious code has been or can be introduced/executed in the product or a user network/information system.
Inform affected users and, where appropriate, all users about AEVs/severe incidents and available mitigation or corrective measures, using structured machine-readable format where applicable.
Technical documentation contains relevant evidence showing product/process compliance with Annex I and at least Annex VII content.
Technical documentation is prepared before market placement and continuously updated as appropriate during the support period.
Where other Union product law also requires technical documentation, maintain a single documentation set containing both sets of required information.
Use an official language of the notified body Member State or another language accepted by that body for conformity documentation/correspondence.
Provide an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on product risks.
No known exploitable vulnerabilities at market placement
Secure-by-default configuration and reset capability
Enable vulnerabilities to be addressed through security updates, including appropriate automatic-update behavior where applicable
Protect against unauthorised access using authentication/identity/access controls and report possible unauthorised access
Protect confidentiality of stored, transmitted and processed data using appropriate state-of-the-art mechanisms
Protect integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration and report corruption
Apply data minimisation to intended product purpose
Protect availability of essential/basic functions including after incidents and against denial-of-service
Minimise negative impact on availability of services provided by other devices/networks
Limit attack surfaces including external interfaces
Reduce incident impact with exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques
Record/monitor security-relevant internal activity with user opt-out mechanism where required
Allow users to securely and permanently remove data/settings and securely transfer data where applicable
Identify/document product vulnerabilities and components and maintain a machine-readable SBOM covering at least top-level dependencies
Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including security updates; separate security/functionality updates where technically feasible
Apply effective and regular product security tests and reviews
After a security update, disclose fixed-vulnerability information, affected product, impact/severity and remediation guidance, subject to justified delayed disclosure
Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy
Facilitate vulnerability information sharing and provide a vulnerability-reporting contact address
Securely distribute updates so vulnerabilities are fixed/mitigated timely and automatically where applicable
Disseminate security updates without delay, generally free of charge, with relevant user advisories
Provide manufacturer name/trade identity plus postal and digital contact details and website where available.
Provide the vulnerability-reporting single point of contact and location of the coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy.
Provide product name/type and additional information enabling unique product identification.
State intended purpose, manufacturer-provided security environment, essential functions and security properties.
Describe known or foreseeable use/misuse circumstances that may lead to significant cybersecurity risks.
Provide the internet address for the EU declaration of conformity where applicable.
State technical security support and the support-period end date.
Provide measures required during initial commissioning and product lifetime for secure use.
Explain how product changes can affect data security.
Explain how security-relevant updates can be installed.
Provide secure decommissioning instructions, including secure removal of user data.
Explain how the default automatic-security-update setting can be turned off where applicable.
For products intended for integration, provide information needed by the integrator for Annex I and Annex VII compliance.
If the manufacturer makes the SBOM available to users, state where it can be accessed.
Technical file states intended purpose
Technical file identifies software versions affecting compliance
For hardware products, technical file includes relevant product illustrations/marking/internal-layout information
Technical file includes Annex II user information/instructions
Document design/development and architecture, including component relationships and integration
Document vulnerability-handling process including SBOM, CVD policy, reporting contact and secure-update distribution solution
Document production and monitoring processes and their validation
Include product cybersecurity risk assessment and Annex I applicability
List applied harmonised standards/common specifications/certification or other technical specifications and explain partial/non-application
Include reports of conformity assessment activities where applicable
Include product and vulnerability-handling test reports
Include EU declaration of conformity
Make SBOM available to market surveillance authority following a reasoned request where needed to check Annex I compliance

scope_note: M11 manufacturer/product-security baseline. Obligation summaries are engineering paraphrases; legal_reference is the controlling locator. This matrix is not a legal opinion or certification.

status_definitions.gap: No sufficient M0-M10 implementation currently exists.
status_definitions.met: Existing M0-M10 implementation and evidence fully satisfy the engineering interpretation for this row.
status_definitions.partial: Reusable M0-M10 implementation exists but CRA-specific semantics/evidence are incomplete.
